a pity I’ve enabled you to cheat the hangman.”"}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "The man snarled, and the bearded man said quietly:"}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "“He would have run no risk of that.”"}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "“Just as you like,” replied Tommy. “I know it’s the fashion to run down

of those young Englishmen not distinguished by any special intellectual
ability, but who are emphatically at their best in what is known as a
“tight place.” Their natural diffidence and caution fall from them like

chance of escape, and behind his casual manner he was racking his brains
furiously."}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "The cold accents of the German took up the conversation:"}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“Have you anything to say before you are put to death as a spy?”"}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“Simply lots of things,” replied Tommy with the same urbanity as before."}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "“Do you deny that you were listening at that door?”"}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "“I do not. I must really apologize--but your conversation was so
interesting that it overcame my scruples.”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“How did you get in?”"}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“Dear old Conrad here.” Tommy smiled deprecatingly at him. “I hesitate

have a better watchdog.”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "Conrad snarled impotently, and said sullenly, as the man with the beard
swung round upon him:"}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "“He gave the word. How was I to know?”"}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "“Yes,” Tommy chimed in. “How was he to know? Don’t blame the poor
fellow. His hasty action has given me the pleasure of seeing you all
face to face.”"}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "He fancied that his words caused some discomposure among the group, but
the watchful German stilled it with a wave of his hand."}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "“Dead men tell no tales,” he said evenly."}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "“Ah,” said Tommy, “but I’m not dead yet!”"}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“You soon will be, my young friend,” said the German."}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "An assenting murmur came from the others."}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "Tommy’s heart beat faster, but his casual pleasantness did not waver."}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "“I think not,” he said firmly. “I should have a great objection to

questions. Let me ask you one for a change. Why didn’t you kill me off
at once before I regained consciousness?”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "The German hesitated, and Tommy seized his advantage."}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“Because you didn’t know how much I knew--and where I obtained that
knowledge. If you kill me now, you never will know.”"}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "But here the emotions of Boris became too much for him. He stepped

get hold of that? You don’t suppose I came up those steps haphazard and

knows pretty ways of making people speak!”"}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "“Bah!” said Tommy scornfully, fighting down a singularly unpleasant
feeling in the pit of his stomach. “You will neither torture me nor kill
me.”"}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "“And why not?” asked Boris."}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“Because you’d kill the goose that lays the golden eggs,” replied Tommy
quietly."}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "There was a momentary pause. It seemed as though Tommy’s persistent
assurance was at last conquering. They were no longer completely sure of
themselves. The man in the shabby clothes stared at Tommy searchingly."}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“He’s bluffing you, Boris,” he said quietly."}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "Tommy hated him. worst of you foreigners. You can’t keep calm. Now, I ask you, do I look
as though I thought there were the least chance of your killing me?”"}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "He looked confidently round, and was glad they could not hear the
persistent beating of his heart which gave the lie to his words."}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "“No,” admitted Boris at last sullenly, “you do not.”"}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "“Thank God, he’s not a mind reader,” thought Tommy. Aloud he pursued his
advantage:"}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "“And why am I so confident? Because I know something that puts me in a

My life and liberty against----” He paused."}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "“Against what?”"}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "The group pressed forward. You could have heard a pin drop."}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "Slowly Tommy spoke."}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "“The papers that Danvers brought over from America in the _Lusitania_.”"}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "The effect of his words was electrical. The German waved them back. He leaned over Tommy, his face purple with
excitement."}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "“_Himmel!_ You have got them, then?”"}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "With magnificent calm Tommy shook his head."}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "“You know where they are?” persisted the German."}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "Again Tommy shook his head. “Not in the least.”"}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "“Then--then----” angry and baffled, the words failed him."}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "Tommy looked round. He saw anger and bewilderment on every face, but his
calm assurance had done its work--no one doubted but that something lay
behind his words."}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“I don’t know where the papers are--but I believe that I can find them.
I have a theory----”"}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "“Pah!”"}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "Tommy raised his hand, and silenced the clamours of disgust."}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "“I call it a theory--but I’m pretty sure of my facts--facts that are
known to no one but myself. In any case what do you lose? If I can
produce the papers--you give me my life and liberty in exchange. Is it a
bargain?”"}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "“And if we refuse?” said the German quietly."}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "Tommy lay back on the couch."}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "“The 29th,” he said thoughtfully, “is less than a fortnight ahead----”"}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "For a moment the German hesitated. Then he made a sign to Conrad."}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "“Take him into the other room.”"}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "For five minutes, Tommy sat on the bed in the dingy room next door. His
heart was beating violently. He had risked all on this throw. How would
they decide? And all the while that this agonized questioning went on
within him, he talked flippantly to Conrad, enraging the cross-grained
doorkeeper to the point of homicidal mania."}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "At last the door opened, and the German called imperiously to Conrad to

frivolously. “That’s right, Conrad, march me in. The prisoner is at the
bar, gentlemen.”"}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "The German was seated once more behind the table. He motioned to Tommy
to sit down opposite to him."}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "“We accept,” he said harshly, “on terms. The papers must be delivered to
us before you go free.”"}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "“Idiot!” said Tommy amiably. “How do you think I can look for them if

did not really think you would agree to that plan. Very well, we must
arrange a compromise. How would it be if you attached little Conrad here
to my person. He’s a faithful fellow, and very ready with the fist.”"}, {"paragraph": 98, "text": "“We prefer,” said the German coldly, “that you should remain here.
One of our number will carry out your instructions minutely. If the
operations are complicated, he will return to you with a report and you
can instruct him further.”"}, {"paragraph": 99, "text": "“You’re tying my hands,” complained Tommy. “It’s a very delicate affair,
and the other fellow will muff it up as likely as not, and then where
shall I be? I don’t believe one of you has got an ounce of tact.”"}, {"paragraph": 100, "text": "The German rapped the table."}, {"paragraph": 101, "text": "“Those are our terms. Otherwise, death!”"}, {"paragraph": 102, "text": "Tommy leaned back wearily."}, {"paragraph": 103, "text": "“I like your style. Curt, but attractive. So be it, then. But one thing
is essential, I must see the girl.”"}, {"paragraph": 104, "text": "“What girl?”"}, {"paragraph": 105, "text": "“Jane Finn, of course.”"}, {"paragraph": 106, "text": "The other looked at him curiously for some minutes, then he said slowly,
and as though choosing his words with care:"}, {"paragraph": 107, "text": "“Do you not know that she can tell you nothing?”"}, {"paragraph": 108, "text": "Tommy’s heart beat a little faster. Would he succeed in coming face to
face with the girl he was seeking?"}, {"paragraph": 109, "text": "“I shall not ask her to tell me anything,” he said quietly. “Not in so
many words, that is.”"}, {"paragraph": 110, "text": "“Then why see her?”"}, {"paragraph": 111, "text": "Tommy paused."}, {"paragraph": 112, "text": "“To watch her face when I ask her one question,” he replied at last."}, {"paragraph": 113, "text": "Again there was a look in the German’s eyes that Tommy did not quite
understand."}, {"paragraph": 114, "text": "“She will not be able to answer your question.”"}, {"paragraph": 115, "text": "“That does not matter. I shall have seen her face when I ask it.”"}, {"paragraph": 116, "text": "“And you think that will tell you anything?” He gave a short
disagreeable laugh. More than ever, Tommy felt that there was a
factor somewhere that he did not understand. The German looked at
him searchingly. “I wonder whether, after all, you know as much as we
think?” he said softly."}, {"paragraph": 117, "text": "Tommy felt his ascendancy less sure than a moment before. His hold had
slipped a little. But he was puzzled. What had he said wrong? He spoke
out on the impulse of the moment."}, {"paragraph": 118, "text": "“There may be things that you know which I do not. I have not pretended
to be aware of all the details of your show. But equally I’ve got
something up my sleeve that _you_ don’t know about. And that’s where I
mean to score. Danvers was a damned clever fellow----” He broke off as
if he had said too much."}, {"paragraph": 119, "text": "But the German’s face had lightened a little."}, {"paragraph": 120, "text": "“Danvers,” he murmured. “I see----” He paused a minute, then waved to

then he would have thrown away a vital chance in mere foolhardiness."}, {"paragraph": 5, "text": "A repetition of the signal knock sounded on the door below, and Tommy,

didn’t roll in. I’d have given the wrong number, and there would have
been the deuce to pay. No, this is the place for me. Hullo, here’s
another knock.”"}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "This visitor proved to be of an entirely different type to the last.
Tommy recognized in him an Irish Sinn Feiner. Certainly Mr. Brown’s
organization was a far-reaching concern. The common criminal, the
well-bred Irish gentleman, the pale Russian, and the efficient German
master of the ceremonies! Truly a strange and sinister gathering! Who
was this man who held in his finger these curiously variegated links of
an unknown chain?"}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "In this case, the procedure was exactly the same. The signal knock, the
demand for a number, and the reply “Correct.”"}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "Two knocks followed in quick succession on the door below. The first man
was quite unknown to Tommy, who put him down as a city clerk. A quiet,
intelligent-looking man, rather shabbily dressed. The second was of the

unknown to the watcher, though he could not for the moment put a name to
it."}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "After his arrival there was a long wait. In fact Tommy concluded that
the gathering was now complete, and was just cautiously creeping out
from his hiding-place, when another knock sent him scuttling back to
cover."}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "This last-comer came up the stairs so quietly that he was almost abreast
of Tommy before the young man had realized his presence."}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "He was a small man, very pale, with a gentle almost womanish air. The
angle of the cheek-bones hinted at his Slavonic ancestry, otherwise
there was nothing to indicate his nationality. As he passed the recess,
he turned his head slowly. The strange light eyes seemed to burn through
the curtain; Tommy could hardly believe that the man did not know he was
there and in spite of himself he shivered. He was no more fanciful than
the majority of young Englishmen, but he could not rid himself of the
impression that some unusually potent force emanated from the man. The
creature reminded him of a venomous snake."}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "A moment later his impression was proved correct. The new-comer knocked
on the door as all had done, but his reception was very different. The
bearded man rose to his feet, and all the others followed suit. The
German came forward and shook hands. His heels clicked together."}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "“We are honoured,” he said. “We are greatly honoured. I much feared that
it would be impossible.”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "The other answered in a low voice that had a kind of hiss in it:"}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“There were difficulties. It will not be possible again, I fear. But one
meeting is essential--to define my policy. I can do nothing without--Mr.
Brown. He is here?”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "The change in the German’s voice was audible as he replied with slight
hesitation:"}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "“We have received a message. It is impossible for him to be present
in person.” He stopped, giving a curious impression of having left the
sentence unfinished."}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "A very slow smile overspread the face of the other. He looked round at a
circle of uneasy faces."}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "“Ah! I understand. I have read of his methods. He works in the dark and
trusts no one. But, all the same, it is possible that he is among us
now....” He looked round him again, and again that expression of fear
swept over the group. Each man seemed eyeing his neighbour doubtfully."}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "The Russian tapped his cheek."}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "“So be it. Let us proceed.”"}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "The German seemed to pull himself together. He indicated the place he
had been occupying at the head of the table. The Russian demurred, but
the other insisted."}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "“It is the only possible place,” he said, “for--Number One. Perhaps
Number Fourteen will shut the door?”"}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "In another moment Tommy was once more confronting bare wooden panels,
and the voices within had sunk once more to a mere undistinguishable
murmur. Tommy became restive. The conversation he had overheard had
stimulated his curiosity. He felt that, by hook or by crook, he must
hear more."}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "There was no sound from below, and it did not seem likely that the
doorkeeper would come upstairs. After listening intently for a minute or
two, he put his head round the curtain. The passage was deserted. Tommy
bent down and removed his shoes, then, leaving them behind the curtain,
he walked gingerly out on his stockinged feet, and kneeling down by
the closed door he laid his ear cautiously to the crack. To his intense
annoyance he could distinguish little more; just a chance word here and
there if a voice was raised, which merely served to whet his curiosity
still farther."}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "He eyed the handle of the door tentatively. Could he turn it by degrees
so gently and imperceptibly that those in the room would notice nothing?
He decided that with great care it could be done. Very slowly, a
fraction of an inch at a time, he moved it round, holding his breath in
his excessive care. A little more--a little more still--would it never
be finished? Ah! at last it would turn no farther."}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "He stayed so for a minute or two, then drew a deep breath, and pressed
it ever so slightly inward. The door did not budge. Tommy was annoyed.
If he had to use too much force, it would almost certainly creak.
He waited until the voices rose a little, then he tried again. Still
nothing happened. He increased the pressure. Had the beastly thing
stuck? Finally, in desperation, he pushed with all his might. But the
door remained firm, and at last the truth dawned upon him. It was locked
or bolted on the inside."}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "For a moment or two Tommy’s indignation got the better of him."}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "“Well, I’m damned!” he said. “What a dirty trick!”"}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "As his indignation cooled, he prepared to face the situation. Clearly
the first thing to be done was to restore the handle to its original
position. If he let it go suddenly, the men inside would be almost
certain to notice it, so, with the same infinite pains, he reversed his
former tactics. All went well, and with a sigh of relief the young man
rose to his feet. There was a certain bulldog tenacity about Tommy that
made him slow to admit defeat. Checkmated for the moment, he was far
from abandoning the conflict. He still intended to hear what was going
on in the locked room. As one plan had failed, he must hunt about for
another."}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "He looked round him. A little farther along the passage on the left was
a second door. He slipped silently along to it. He listened for a moment
or two, then tried the handle. It yielded, and he slipped inside."}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "The room, which was untenanted, was furnished as a bedroom. Like
everything else in the house, the furniture was falling to pieces, and
the dirt was, if anything, more abundant."}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "But what interested Tommy was the thing he had hoped to find, a
communicating door between the two rooms, up on the left by the window.
Carefully closing the door into the passage behind him, he stepped
across to the other and examined it closely. The bolt was shot across
it. It was very rusty, and had clearly not been used for some time. By
gently wriggling it to and fro, Tommy managed to draw it back without
making too much noise. Then he repeated his former manœuvres with the
handle--this time with complete success. The door swung open--a crack,
a mere fraction, but enough for Tommy to hear what went on. There was a
velvet _portière_ on the inside of this door which prevented him from
seeing, but he was able to recognize the voices with a reasonable amount
of accuracy."}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "The Sinn Feiner was speaking. His rich Irish voice was unmistakable:"}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "“That’s all very well. But more money is essential. No money--no

its foundations.”"}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "There was a pause, and then came the soft, sibilant accents of Number
One:"}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "“Good! You shall have the money. are getting a mite difficult. There’s not the sympathy there was, and
a growing disposition to let the Irish settle their own affairs without
interference from America.”"}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "Tommy felt that Boris had shrugged his shoulders as he answered:"}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“Does that matter, since the money only nominally comes from the

satisfactorily, Boris?”"}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "“I think so.”"}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "“That is good. An official denial from Moscow will be forthcoming if

hopes were high. The plan seemed to him simple but excellent."}, {"paragraph": 6, "text": "Time went on, but Conrad did not appear. Night and day were the same

degree of accuracy, informed him that it was nine o’clock in the

deserted him, and he flung himself on the bed to seek consolation in

wondered vaguely where he was. Then he remembered, and looked at his
watch. It was eight o’clock."}, {"paragraph": 8, "text": "“It’s either early morning tea or breakfast,” deduced the young man,

know? Elementary, my dear Watson--the smell of onions is unmistakable.”"}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "“Talk away,” grunted the man. “It’s little enough time you’ll have to
talk in, maybe.”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "The remark was unpleasant in its suggestion, but Tommy ignored it. He
sat down at the table."}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“Retire, varlet,” he said, with a wave of his hand. “Prate not to thy
betters.”"}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "That evening Tommy sat on the bed, and cogitated deeply. Would Conrad
again accompany the girl? If he did not, should he risk trying to make
an ally of her? He decided that he must leave no stone unturned. His
position was desperate."}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "At eight o’clock the familiar sound of the key turning made him spring
to his feet. The girl was alone."}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "“Shut the door,” he commanded. “I want to speak to you.” She obeyed."}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "“Look here, Annette, I want you to help me get out of this.” She shook
her head."}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "“Impossible. There are three of them on the floor below.”"}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "“Oh!” Tommy was secretly grateful for the information. “But you would
help me if you could?”"}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "“No, monsieur.”"}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "“Why not?”"}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "The girl hesitated."}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "“I think--they are my own people. You have spied upon them. They are
quite right to keep you here.”"}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "“They’re a bad lot, Annette. If you’ll help me, I’ll take you away from
the lot of them. And you’d probably get a good whack of money.”"}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "But the girl merely shook her head."}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“I dare not, monsieur; I am afraid of them.”"}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "She turned away."}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“Wouldn’t you do anything to help another girl?” cried Tommy. “She’s
about your age too. Won’t you save her from their clutches?”"}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "“You mean Jane Finn?”"}, {"paragraph": 55, "text": "“Yes.”"}, {"paragraph": 56, "text": "“It is her you came here to look for? Yes?”"}, {"paragraph": 57, "text": "“That’s it.”"}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "The girl looked at him, then passed her hand across her forehead."}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "“Jane Finn. Always I hear that name. It is familiar.”"}, {"paragraph": 60, "text": "Tommy came forward eagerly."}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "“You must know _something_ about her?”"}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "But the girl turned away abruptly."}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "“I know nothing--only the name.” She walked towards the door. Suddenly
she uttered a cry. Tommy stared. She had caught sight of the picture
he had laid against the wall the night before. For a moment he caught a
look of terror in her eyes. As inexplicably it changed to relief. Then
abruptly she went out of the room. Tommy could make nothing of it. Did
she fancy that he had meant to attack her with it? Surely not. He rehung
the picture on the wall thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "Three more days went by in dreary inaction. Tommy felt the strain
telling on his nerves. He saw no one but Conrad and Annette, and the
girl had become dumb. She spoke only in monosyllables. A kind of dark
suspicion smouldered in her eyes. Tommy felt that if this solitary
confinement went on much longer he would go mad. He gathered from Conrad
that they were waiting for orders from “Mr. Brown.” Perhaps, thought
Tommy, he was abroad or away, and they were obliged to wait for his
return."}, {"paragraph": 65, "text": "But the evening of the third day brought a rude awakening."}, {"paragraph": 66, "text": "It was barely seven o’clock when he heard the tramp of footsteps outside
in the passage. In another minute the door was flung open. Conrad
entered. With him was the evil-looking Number 14. Tommy’s heart sank at
the sight of them."}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "“Evenin’, gov’nor,” said the man with a leer. “Got those ropes, mate?”"}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "The silent Conrad produced a length of fine cord. The next minute Number
14’s hands, horribly dexterous, were winding the cord round his limbs,
while Conrad held him down."}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "“What the devil----?” began Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "But the slow, speechless grin of the silent Conrad froze the words on
his lips."}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "Number 14 proceeded deftly with his task. In another minute Tommy was a
mere helpless bundle. Then at last Conrad spoke:"}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "“Thought you’d bluffed us, did you? With what you knew, and what you
didn’t know. Bargained with us! And all the time it was bluff! Bluff!
You know less than a kitten. But your number’s up now all right, you
b---- swine.”"}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "Tommy lay silent. There was nothing to say. He had failed. Somehow
or other the omnipotent Mr. Brown had seen through his pretensions.
Suddenly a thought occurred to him."}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "“A very good speech, Conrad,” he said approvingly. “But wherefore the
bonds and fetters? Why not let this kind gentleman here cut my throat
without delay?”"}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "“Garn,” said Number 14 unexpectedly. “Think we’re as green as to do you
in here, and have the police nosing round? Not ‘alf! We’ve ordered the
carriage for your lordship to-morrow mornin’, but in the meantime we’re
not taking any chances, see!”"}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "“Nothing,” said Tommy, “could be plainer than your words--unless it was
your face.”"}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "“Stow it,” said Number 14."}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“With pleasure,” replied Tommy. “You’re making a sad mistake--but yours
will be the loss.”"}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "“You don’t kid us that way again,” said Number 14. “Talking as though
you were still at the blooming _Ritz_, aren’t you?”"}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "Tommy made no reply. He was engaged in wondering how Mr. Brown had
discovered his identity. He decided that Tuppence, in the throes of
anxiety, had gone to the police, and that his disappearance having been
made public the gang had not been slow to put two and two together."}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "The two men departed and the door slammed. Tommy was left to his
meditations. They were not pleasant ones. Already his limbs felt cramped
and stiff. He was utterly helpless, and he could see no hope anywhere."}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "About an hour had passed when he heard the key softly turned, and the
door opened. It was Annette. Tommy’s heart beat a little faster. He had
forgotten the girl. Was it possible that she had come to his help?"}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "Suddenly he heard Conrad’s voice:"}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "“Come out of it, Annette. He doesn’t want any supper to-night.”"}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "“Oui, oui, je sais bien. But I must take the other tray. We need the
things on it.”"}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "“Well, hurry up,” growled Conrad."}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "Without looking at Tommy the girl went over to the table, and picked up
the tray. She raised a hand and turned out the light."}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "“Curse you”--Conrad had come to the door--“why did you do that?”"}, {"paragraph": 89, "text": "“I always turn it out. You should have told me. Shall I relight it,
Monsieur Conrad?”"}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "“No, come on out of it.”"}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "“Le beau petit monsieur,” cried Annette, pausing by the bed in the
darkness. “You have tied him up well, _hein?_ He is like a trussed
chicken!” The frank amusement in her tone jarred on the boy; but at
that moment, to his amazement, he felt her hand running lightly over
his bonds, and something small and cold was pressed into the palm of his
hand."}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "“Come on, Annette.”"}, {"paragraph": 93, "text": "“Mais me voilà.”"}, {"paragraph": 94, "text": "The door shut. Tommy heard Conrad say:"}, {"paragraph": 95, "text": "“Lock it and give me the key.”"}, {"paragraph": 96, "text": "The footsteps died away. Tommy lay petrified with amazement. The object
Annette had thrust into his hand was a small penknife, the blade open.
From the way she had studiously avoided looking at him, and her action
with the light, he came to the conclusion that the room was overlooked.
There must be a peep-hole somewhere in the walls. Remembering how
guarded she had always been in her manner, he saw that he had probably
been under observation all the time. Had he said anything to give
himself away? Hardly. He had revealed a wish to escape and a desire
to find Jane Finn, but nothing that could have given a clue to his
own identity. True, his question to Annette had proved that he was
personally unacquainted with Jane Finn, but he had never pretended
otherwise. The question now was, did Annette really know more? Were her
denials intended primarily for the listeners? On that point he could
come to no conclusion."}, {"paragraph": 97, "text": "But there was a more vital question that drove out all others. Could he,
bound as he was, manage to cut his bonds? He essayed cautiously to
rub the open blade up and down on the cord that bound his two wrists
together. It was an awkward business, and drew a smothered “Ow” of pain
from him as the knife cut into his wrist. But slowly and doggedly he
went on sawing to and fro. He cut the flesh badly, but at last he felt
the cord slacken. With his hands free, the rest was easy. Five minutes
later he stood upright with some difficulty, owing to the cramp in his
limbs. His first care was to bind up his bleeding wrist. Then he sat on
the edge of the bed to think. Conrad had taken the key of the door, so
he could expect little more assistance from Annette. The only outlet
from the room was the door, consequently he would perforce have to wait
until the two men returned to fetch him. But when they did.... Tommy
smiled! Moving with infinite caution in the dark room, he found and
unhooked the famous picture. He felt an economical pleasure that his
first plan would not be wasted. There was now nothing to do but to wait.
He waited."}, {"paragraph": 98, "text": "The night passed slowly. Tommy lived through an eternity of hours, but
at last he heard footsteps. He stood upright, drew a deep breath, and
clutched the picture firmly."}, {"paragraph": 99, "text": "The door opened. A faint light streamed in from outside. Conrad went
straight towards the gas to light it. Tommy deeply regretted that it was
he who had entered first. It would have been pleasant to get even with
Conrad. Number 14 followed. As he stepped across the threshold, Tommy
brought the picture down with terrific force on his head. Number 14 went
down amidst a stupendous crash of broken glass. In a minute Tommy had
slipped out and pulled to the door. The key was in the lock. He turned
it and withdrew it just as Conrad hurled himself against the door from
the inside with a volley of curses."}, {"paragraph": 100, "text": "For a moment Tommy hesitated. There was the sound of some one stirring
on the floor below. Then the German’s voice came up the stairs."}, {"paragraph": 101, "text": "“Gott im Himmel! Conrad, what is it?”"}, {"paragraph": 102, "text": "Tommy felt a small hand thrust into his. Beside him stood Annette. She
pointed up a rickety ladder that apparently led to some attics."}, {"paragraph": 103, "text": "“Quick--up here!” She dragged him after her up the ladder. In another
moment they were standing in a dusty garret littered with lumber. Tommy
looked round."}, {"paragraph": 104, "text": "“This won’t do. It’s a regular trap. There’s no way out.”"}, {"paragraph": 105, "text": "“Hush! Wait.” The girl put her finger to her lips. She crept to the top
of the ladder and listened."}, {"paragraph": 106, "text": "The banging and beating on the door was terrific. The German and another
were trying to force the door in. Annette explained in a whisper:"}, {"paragraph": 107, "text": "“They will think you are still inside. They cannot hear what Conrad
says. The door is too thick.”"}, {"paragraph": 108, "text": "“I thought you could hear what went on in the room?”"}, {"paragraph": 109, "text": "“There is a peep-hole into the next room. It was clever of you to guess.
But they will not think of that--they are only anxious to get in.”"}, {"paragraph": 110, "text": "“Yes--but look here----”"}, {"paragraph": 111, "text": "“Leave it to me.” She bent down. To his amazement, Tommy saw that she
was fastening the end of a long piece of string to the handle of a big
cracked jug. She arranged it carefully, then turned to Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 112, "text": "“Have you the key of the door?”"}, {"paragraph": 113, "text": "“Yes.”"}, {"paragraph": 114, "text": "“Give it to me.”"}, {"paragraph": 115, "text": "He handed it to her."}, {"paragraph": 116, "text": "“I am going down. Do you think you can go halfway, and then swing
yourself down _behind_ the ladder, so that they will not see you?”"}, {"paragraph": 117, "text": "Tommy nodded."}, {"paragraph": 118, "text": "“There’s a big cupboard in the shadow of the landing. Stand behind it.
Take the end of this string in your hand. When I’ve let the others out--
_pull! _”"}, {"paragraph": 119, "text": "Before he had time to ask her anything more, she had flitted lightly
down the ladder and was in the midst of the group with a loud cry:"}, {"paragraph": 120, "text": "“Mon Dieu! Mon Dieu! Qu’est-ce qu’il y a?”"}, {"paragraph": 121, "text": "The German turned on her with an oath."}, {"paragraph": 122, "text": "“Get out of this. Go to your room!”"}, {"paragraph": 123, "text": "Very cautiously Tommy swung himself down the back of the ladder. So
long as they did not turn round ... all was well. He crouched behind the
cupboard. They were still between him and the stairs."}, {"paragraph": 124, "text": "“Ah!” Annette appeared to stumble over something. She stooped. “Mon
Dieu, voilà la clef!”"}, {"paragraph": 125, "text": "The German snatched it from her. He unlocked the door. Conrad stumbled
out, swearing."}, {"paragraph": 126, "text": "“Where is he? Have you got him?”"}, {"paragraph": 127, "text": "“We have seen no one,” said the German sharply. His face paled. “Who do
you mean?”"}, {"paragraph": 128, "text": "Conrad gave vent to another oath."}, {"paragraph": 129, "text": "“He’s got away.”"}, {"paragraph": 130, "text": "“Impossible. He would have passed us.”"}, {"paragraph": 131, "text": "At that moment, with an ecstatic smile Tommy pulled the string. A crash
of crockery came from the attic above. In a trice the men were pushing
each other up the rickety ladder and had disappeared into the darkness
above."}, {"paragraph": 132, "text": "Quick as a flash Tommy leapt from his hiding-place and dashed down the
stairs, pulling the girl with him. There was no one in the hall. He
fumbled over the bolts and chain. At last they yielded, the door swung
open. He turned. Annette had disappeared."}, {"paragraph": 133, "text": "Tommy stood spell-bound. Had she run upstairs again? What madness
possessed her! He fumed with impatience, but he stood his ground. He
would not go without her."}, {"paragraph": 134, "text": "And suddenly there was an outcry overhead, an exclamation from the
German, and then Annette’s voice, clear and high:"}, {"paragraph": 135, "text": "“Ma foi, he has escaped! And quickly! Who would have thought it?”"}, {"paragraph": 136, "text": "Tommy still stood rooted to the ground. Was that a command to him to go?
He fancied it was."}, {"paragraph": 137, "text": "And then, louder still, the words floated down to him:"}, {"paragraph": 138, "text": "“This is a terrible house. I want to go back to Marguerite. To
Marguerite. _To Marguerite!_”"}, {"paragraph": 139, "text": "Tommy had run back to the stairs. She wanted him to go and leave her.
But why? At all costs he must try and get her away with him. Then his
heart sank. Conrad was leaping down the stairs, uttering a savage cry at
the sight of him. After him came the others."}, {"paragraph": 140, "text": "Tommy stopped Conrad’s rush with a straight blow with his fist. It
caught the other on the point of the jaw and he fell like a log. The
second man tripped over his body and fell. From higher up the staircase
there was a flash, and a bullet grazed Tommy’s ear. He realized that
it would be good for his health to get out of this house as soon as
possible. As regards Annette he could do nothing. He had got even with
Conrad, which was one satisfaction. The blow had been a good one."}, {"paragraph": 141, "text": "He leapt for the door, slamming it behind him. The square was deserted.
In front of the house was a baker’s van. Evidently he was to have been
taken out of London in that, and his body found many miles from the
house in Soho. The driver jumped to the pavement and tried to bar
Tommy’s way. Again Tommy’s fist shot out, and the driver sprawled on the
pavement."}, {"paragraph": 142, "text": "Tommy took to his heels and ran--none too soon. The front door opened
and a hail of bullets followed him. Fortunately none of them hit him. He
turned the corner of the square."}, {"paragraph": 143, "text": "“There’s one thing,” he thought to himself, “they can’t go on shooting.
They’ll have the police after them if they do. I wonder they dared to
there.”"}, {"paragraph": 144, "text": "He heard the footsteps of his pursuers behind him, and redoubled his own
pace. Once he got out of these by-ways he would be safe. There would be
a policeman about somewhere--not that he really wanted to invoke the aid
of the police if he could possibly do without it. It meant explanations,
and general awkwardness. In another moment he had reason to bless his
luck. He stumbled over a prostrate figure, which started up with a yell
of alarm and dashed off down the street. Tommy drew back into a doorway.
In a minute he had the pleasure of seeing his two pursuers, of whom the
German was one, industriously tracking down the red herring!"}, {"paragraph": 145, "text": "Tommy sat down quietly on the doorstep and allowed a few moments to
elapse while he recovered his breath. Then he strolled gently in the
opposite direction. He glanced at his watch. It was a little after
half-past five. It was rapidly growing light. At the next corner he
passed a policeman. The policeman cast a suspicious eye on him. Tommy
felt slightly offended. Then, passing his hand over his face, he
laughed. He had not shaved or washed for three days! What a guy he must
look."}, {"paragraph": 146, "text": "He betook himself without more ado to a Turkish Bath establishment which
he knew to be open all night. He emerged into the busy daylight feeling
himself once more, and able to make plans."}, {"paragraph": 147, "text": "First of all, he must have a square meal. He had eaten nothing since
midday yesterday. He turned into an A.B.C. shop and ordered eggs and
bacon and coffee. Whilst he ate, he read a morning paper propped up
in front of him. Suddenly he stiffened. There was a long article on
Kramenin, who was described as the “man behind Bolshevism” in Russia,
and who had just arrived in London--some thought as an unofficial envoy.
His career was sketched lightly, and it was firmly asserted that he,
and not the figurehead leaders, had been the author of the Russian
Revolution."}, {"paragraph": 148, "text": "In the centre of the page was his portrait."}, {"paragraph": 149, "text": "“So that’s who Number 1 is,” said Tommy with his mouth full of eggs and
bacon. “Not a doubt about it, I must push on.”"}, {"paragraph": 150, "text": "He paid for his breakfast, and betook himself to Whitehall. There he
sent up his name, and the message that it was urgent. A few minutes
later he was in the presence of the man who did not here go by the name
of “Mr. Carter.” There was a frown on his face."}, {"paragraph": 151, "text": "“Look here, you’ve no business to come asking for me in this way. I
thought that was distinctly understood?”"}, {"paragraph": 152, "text": "“It was, sir. But I judged it important to lose no time.”"}, {"paragraph": 153, "text": "And as briefly and succinctly as possible he detailed the experiences of
the last few days."}, {"paragraph": 154, "text": "Half-way through, Mr. Carter interrupted him to give a few cryptic
orders through the telephone. All traces of displeasure had now left his
face. He nodded energetically when Tommy had finished."}, {"paragraph": 155, "text": "“Quite right. Every moment’s of value. Fear we shall be too late anyway.
They wouldn’t wait. Would clear out at once. Still, they may have left
something behind them that will be a clue. You say you’ve recognized
Number 1 to be Kramenin? That’s important. We want something against him
badly to prevent the Cabinet falling on his neck too freely. What about
the others? You say two faces were familiar to you? One’s a Labour man,
you think? Just look through these photos, and see if you can spot him.”"}, {"paragraph": 156, "text": "A minute later, Tommy held one up. Mr. Carter exhibited some surprise."}, {"paragraph": 157, "text": "“Ah, Westway! Shouldn’t have thought it. Poses as being moderate. As for
the other fellow, I think I can give a good guess.” He handed another
photograph to Tommy, and smiled at the other’s exclamation. “I’m right,
then. Who is he? Irishman. Prominent Unionist M.P. All a blind, of
course. We’ve suspected it--but couldn’t get any proof. Yes, you’ve done
very well, young man. The 29th, you say, is the date. That gives us very
little time--very little time indeed.”"}, {"paragraph": 158, "text": "“But----” Tommy hesitated."}, {"paragraph": 159, "text": "Mr. Carter read his thoughts."}, {"paragraph": 160, "text": "“We can deal with the General Strike menace, I think. It’s a
toss-up--but we’ve got a sporting chance! But if that draft treaty turns
up--we’re done. England will be plunged in anarchy. Ah, what’s that?
The car? Come on, Beresford, we’ll go and have a look at this house of
yours.”"}, {"paragraph": 161, "text": "Two constables were on duty in front of the house in Soho. An inspector
reported to Mr. Carter in a low voice. The latter turned to Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 162, "text": "“The birds have flown--as we thought. We might as well go over it.”"}, {"paragraph": 163, "text": "Going over the deserted house seemed to Tommy to partake of the
character of a dream. Everything was just as it had been. The prison
room with the crooked pictures, the broken jug in the attic, the meeting
room with its long table. But nowhere was there a trace of papers.
Everything of that kind had either been destroyed or taken away. And
there was no sign of Annette."}, {"paragraph": 164, "text": "“What you tell me about the girl puzzled me,” said Mr. Carter. “You
believe that she deliberately went back?”"}, {"paragraph": 165, "text": "“It would seem so, sir. She ran upstairs while I was getting the door
open.”"}, {"paragraph": 166, "text": "“H’m, she must belong to the gang, then; but, being a woman, didn’t feel
like standing by to see a personable young man killed. But evidently
she’s in with them, or she wouldn’t have gone back.”"}, {"paragraph": 167, "text": "“I can’t believe she’s really one of them, sir. She--seemed so
different----”"}, {"paragraph": 168, "text": "“Good-looking, I suppose?” said Mr. Carter with a smile that made Tommy
flush to the roots of his hair. He admitted Annette’s beauty rather
shamefacedly."}, {"paragraph": 169, "text": "“By the way,” observed Mr. Carter, “have you shown yourself to Miss
Tuppence yet? She’s been bombarding me with letters about you.”"}, {"paragraph": 170, "text": "“Tuppence? I was afraid she might get a bit rattled. Did she go to the
police?”"}, {"paragraph": 171, "text": "Mr. Carter shook his head."}, {"paragraph": 172, "text": "“Then I wonder how they twigged me.”"}, {"paragraph": 173, "text": "Mr. Carter looked inquiringly at him, and Tommy explained. The other
nodded thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 174, "text": "“True, that’s rather a curious point. Unless the mention of the _Ritz_
was an accidental remark?”"}, {"paragraph": 175, "text": "“It might have been, sir. But they must have found out about me suddenly
in some way.”"}, {"paragraph": 176, "text": "“Well,” said Mr. Carter, looking round him, “there’s nothing more to be
done here. What about some lunch with me?”"}, {"paragraph": 177, "text": "“Thanks awfully, sir. But I think I’d better get back and rout out
Tuppence.”"}, {"paragraph": 178, "text": "“Of course. Give her my kind regards and tell her not to believe you’re
killed too readily next time.”"}, {"paragraph": 179, "text": "Tommy grinned."}, {"paragraph": 180, "text": "“I take a lot of killing, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 181, "text": "“So I perceive,” said Mr. Carter dryly. “Well, good-bye. Remember you’re
a marked man now, and take reasonable care of yourself.”"}, {"paragraph": 182, "text": "“Thank you, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 183, "text": "Hailing a taxi briskly Tommy stepped in, and was swiftly borne to the
_Ritz_, dwelling the while on the pleasurable anticipation of startling
Tuppence."}, {"paragraph": 184, "text": "“Wonder what she’s been up to. Dogging ‘Rita’ most likely. By the way,
I suppose that’s who Annette meant by Marguerite. I didn’t get it at the
time.” The thought saddened him a little, for it seemed to prove that
Mrs. Vandemeyer and the girl were on intimate terms."}, {"paragraph": 185, "text": "The taxi drew up at the _Ritz_. Tommy burst into its sacred portals
eagerly, but his enthusiasm received a check. He was informed that Miss
Cowley had gone out a quarter of an hour ago."}], "018.revision": [{"paragraph": 1, "text": "The troubles of the future, however, soon faded before the troubles of the present. And of these, the most immediate and pressing was that of hunger. He regretfully recognized the fact that he would not make a success of a hunger strike."}, {"paragraph": 2, "text": "“It’s that sour-faced brute Conrad,” he decided. “This is just a bit of spite on his part. I’m certain of it.”"}, {"paragraph": 3, "text": "Why not wait in ambush for Conrad behind the door, and when he entered bring down one of the decrepit pictures smartly on to his head? Intoxicated by his plan, Tommy gently unhooked the picture of the Devil and Faust, and settled himself in position."}, {"paragraph": 4, "text": "At ten o’clock hope deserted him, and he flung himself on the bed. In five minutes his woes were forgotten."}, {"paragraph": 5, "text": "The sound of the key turning in the lock awoke him. It was eight o’clock."}, {"paragraph": 6, "text": "The door swung open. It was not Conrad who entered, but a girl. She carried a tray which she set down on the table."}, {"paragraph": 7, "text": "Tommy decided at once that she was one of the most beautiful girls he had ever seen. Her hair was a full rich brown, with sudden glints of gold in it as though there were imprisoned sunbeams struggling in its depths. Her eyes, set wide apart, were hazel, a golden hazel that again recalled a memory of sunbeams."}, {"paragraph": 8, "text": "A delirious thought shot through Tommy’s mind."}, {"paragraph": 9, "text": "“Are you Jane Finn?” he asked breathlessly."}, {"paragraph": 10, "text": "The girl shook her head wonderingly."}, {"paragraph": 11, "text": "“My name is Annette, monsieur.”"}, {"paragraph": 12, "text": "She spoke in a soft, broken English."}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "The tray held a loaf, some margarine, and a jug of coffee. The girl turned away to the door."}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "“Wait a sec,” cried Tommy. “What are you doing in this house?”"}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "“I do the _service_, monsieur.”"}, {"paragraph": 16, "text": "“I see,” said Tommy. “You know what I asked you just now. Have you ever heard that name?”"}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "“I have heard people speak of Jane Finn, I think.”"}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“You don’t know where she is? She’s not in this house, for instance?”"}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“Oh no, monsieur. I must go now--they will be waiting for me.”"}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "She hurried out. The key turned in the lock."}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "At one o’clock Annette reappeared, but this time Conrad accompanied her."}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“Good morning,” said Tommy amiably. “You have _not_ used Pear’s soap, I see.”"}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“Talk away,” grunted the man. “It’s little enough time you’ll have to talk in, maybe.”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "That evening Tommy cogitated deeply. Should he risk trying to make an ally of the girl?"}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "At eight o’clock the key turned. The girl was alone."}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "“Shut the door,” he commanded. “I want to speak to you.” She obeyed."}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "“Look here, Annette, I want you to help me get out of this.” She shook her head."}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "“Impossible. There are three of them on the floor below.”"}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "“But you would help me if you could?”"}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“No, monsieur.”"}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "“Why not?”"}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "“I think--they are my own people. You have spied upon them. They are quite right to keep you here.”"}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "“They’re a bad lot, Annette. If you’ll help me, I’ll take you away from the lot of them.”"}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "“I dare not, monsieur; I am afraid of them.”"}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "“Won’t you save another girl from their clutches?” cried Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "“You mean Jane Finn?”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "The girl looked at him, then passed her hand across her forehead."}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“Jane Finn. Always I hear that name. It is familiar.”"}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "But the girl turned away abruptly."}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "“I know nothing--only the name.” She walked towards the door. Suddenly she uttered a cry. She had caught sight of the picture he had laid against the wall the night before. For a moment he caught a look of terror in her eyes. As inexplicably it changed to relief. He rehung the picture on the wall thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "Three more days went by in dreary inaction. He saw no one but Conrad and Annette, and the girl had become dumb. A kind of dark suspicion smouldered in her eyes. He gathered from Conrad that they were waiting for orders from “Mr. Brown.”"}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "But the evening of the third day brought a rude awakening."}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "It was barely seven o’clock when the door was flung open. Conrad entered. With him was the evil-looking Number 14."}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "“Evenin’, gov’nor,” said the man with a leer. “Got those ropes, mate?”"}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "The silent Conrad produced a length of fine cord. The next minute Number 14’s hands, horribly dexterous, were winding the cord round his limbs, while Conrad held him down. Then at last Conrad spoke:"}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "“Thought you’d bluffed us, did you? With what you knew, and what you didn’t know. Bargained with us! And all the time it was bluff! Bluff! You know less than a kitten. But your number’s up now all right, you b---- swine.”"}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "Tommy lay silent. He had failed. Suddenly a thought occurred to him."}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "“A very good speech, Conrad,” he said approvingly. “But wherefore the bonds and fetters? Why not let this kind gentleman here cut my throat without delay?”"}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "“Garn,” said Number 14 unexpectedly. “Think we’re as green as to do you in here, and have the police nosing round? Not ‘alf! We’ve ordered the carriage for your lordship to-morrow mornin’, but in the meantime we’re not taking any chances, see!”"}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "“Nothing,” said Tommy, “could be plainer than your words--unless it was your face.”"}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“You don’t kid us that way again,” said Number 14. “Talking as though you were still at the blooming _Ritz_, aren’t you?”"}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "Tommy made no reply. He was engaged in wondering how Mr. Brown had discovered his identity. He decided that Tuppence, in the throes of anxiety, had gone to the police, and that his disappearance having been made public the gang had not been slow to put two and two together."}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "The two men departed and the door slammed. He was utterly helpless."}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "About an hour had passed when the key was softly turned. It was Annette."}, {"paragraph": 55, "text": "Suddenly he heard Conrad’s voice:"}, {"paragraph": 56, "text": "“Come out of it, Annette. He doesn’t want any supper to-night.”"}, {"paragraph": 57, "text": "Without looking at Tommy the girl went over to the table, and picked up the tray. She raised a hand and turned out the light."}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "“Le beau petit monsieur,” cried Annette, pausing by the bed in the darkness. “You have tied him up well, _hein?_ He is like a trussed chicken!” The frank amusement in her tone jarred on the boy; but at that moment, to his amazement, he felt her hand running lightly over his bonds, and something small and cold was pressed into the palm of his hand."}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "The door shut. Tommy heard Conrad say:"}, {"paragraph": 60, "text": "“Lock it and give me the key.”"}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "The object Annette had thrust into his hand was a small penknife, the blade open. From the way she had studiously avoided looking at him, and her action with the light, he came to the conclusion that the room was overlooked. There must be a peep-hole somewhere in the walls. He saw that he had probably been under observation all the time. Were her denials intended primarily for the listeners? On that point he could come to no conclusion."}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "Could he, bound as he was, manage to cut his bonds? He essayed cautiously to rub the open blade up and down on the cord that bound his wrists. It was an awkward business, and drew a smothered “Ow” of pain from him as the knife cut into his wrist. He cut the flesh badly, but at last he felt the cord slacken. The only outlet was the door, and he would have to wait until the two men returned to fetch him. But when they did.... Tommy smiled! Moving with infinite caution in the dark room, he found and unhooked the famous picture. He waited."}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "The night passed slowly, but at last he heard footsteps. He clutched the picture firmly."}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "The door opened. Conrad went straight towards the gas to light it. Number 14 followed. As he stepped across the threshold, Tommy brought the picture down with terrific force on his head. Number 14 went down amidst a stupendous crash of broken glass. In a minute Tommy had slipped out and pulled to the door. The key was in the lock. He turned it and withdrew it just as Conrad hurled himself against the door from the inside with a volley of curses."}, {"paragraph": 65, "text": "The German’s voice came up the stairs."}, {"paragraph": 66, "text": "“Gott im Himmel! Conrad, what is it?”"}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "Tommy felt a small hand thrust into his. Beside him stood Annette. She pointed up a rickety ladder that apparently led to some attics."}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "“Quick--up here!” She dragged him after her up the ladder into a dusty garret littered with lumber."}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "“Hush! Wait.” She crept to the top of the ladder and listened. The German and another were trying to force the door in. Annette explained in a whisper:"}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "“They will think you are still inside. They cannot hear what Conrad says. The door is too thick.”"}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "“I thought you could hear what went on in the room?”"}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "“There is a peep-hole into the next room. It was clever of you to guess. But they will not think of that--they are only anxious to get in.”"}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "“Leave it to me.” To his amazement, Tommy saw that she was fastening the end of a long piece of string to the handle of a big cracked jug."}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "“Have you the key of the door? Give it to me.”"}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "He handed it to her."}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "“I am going down. Do you think you can go halfway, and then swing yourself down _behind_ the ladder, so that they will not see you? There’s a big cupboard in the shadow of the landing. Stand behind it. Take the end of this string in your hand. When I’ve let the others out--_pull!_”"}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "She had flitted lightly down the ladder and was in the midst of the group with a loud cry:"}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“Mon Dieu! Mon Dieu! Qu’est-ce qu’il y a?”"}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "Very cautiously Tommy swung himself down the back of the ladder and crouched behind the cupboard."}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "“Ah!” Annette appeared to stumble over something. She stooped. “Mon Dieu, voilà la clef!”"}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "The German snatched it from her. He unlocked the door. Conrad stumbled out, swearing."}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "“Where is he? Have you got him?”"}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "At that moment, with an ecstatic smile Tommy pulled the string. A crash of crockery came from the attic above. In a trice the men were pushing each other up the rickety ladder and had disappeared into the darkness above."}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "Quick as a flash Tommy leapt from his hiding-place and dashed down the stairs, pulling the girl with him. There was no one in the hall. He fumbled over the bolts and chain. At last the door swung open. He turned. Annette had disappeared."}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "And suddenly there was an outcry overhead, an exclamation from the German, and then Annette’s voice, clear and high:"}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "“Ma foi, he has escaped! And quickly! Who would have thought it?”"}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "And then, louder still, the words floated down to him:"}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "“This is a terrible house. I want to go back to Marguerite. To Marguerite. _To Marguerite!_”"}, {"paragraph": 89, "text": "Tommy had run back to the stairs. Then his heart sank. Conrad was leaping down the stairs, uttering a savage cry at the sight of him. After him came the others."}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "Tommy stopped Conrad’s rush with a straight blow that caught him on the point of the jaw, and he fell like a log. From higher up the staircase there was a flash, and a bullet grazed Tommy’s ear. As regards Annette he could do nothing."}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "He leapt for the door, slamming it behind him. In front of the house was a baker’s van. The driver jumped to the pavement and tried to bar Tommy’s way. Again Tommy’s fist shot out, and the driver sprawled on the pavement."}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "Tommy took to his heels and ran--none too soon. A hail of bullets followed him. He turned the corner of the square, the footsteps of his pursuers behind him. Then he stumbled over a prostrate figure, which started up with a yell of alarm and dashed off down the street. Tommy drew back into a doorway, and had the pleasure of seeing his two pursuers, of whom the German was one, industriously tracking down the red herring!"}, {"paragraph": 93, "text": "After a Turkish Bath he turned into an A.B.C. shop and ordered eggs and bacon. Whilst he ate, he read a morning paper. Suddenly he stiffened. There was a long article on Kramenin, described as the “man behind Bolshevism” in Russia, who had just arrived in London. In the centre of the page was his portrait."}, {"paragraph": 94, "text": "“So that’s who Number 1 is,” said Tommy with his mouth full of eggs and bacon. “Not a doubt about it, I must push on.”"}, {"paragraph": 95, "text": "He betook himself to Whitehall, sent up his name, and the message that it was urgent. A few minutes later he was in the presence of the man who did not here go by the name of “Mr. Carter.” There was a frown on his face."}, {"paragraph": 96, "text": "“Look here, you’ve no business to come asking for me in this way. I thought that was distinctly understood?”"}, {"paragraph": 97, "text": "“It was, sir. But I judged it important to lose no time.”"}, {"paragraph": 98, "text": "And as briefly as possible he detailed the experiences of the last few days. Half-way through, Mr. Carter interrupted him to give a few cryptic orders through the telephone. All traces of displeasure had now left his face."}, {"paragraph": 99, "text": "“Quite right. Every moment’s of value. You say you’ve recognized Number 1 to be Kramenin? That’s important. You say two faces were familiar to you? Just look through these photos.”"}, {"paragraph": 100, "text": "Tommy held one up."}, {"paragraph": 101, "text": "“Ah, Westway! Shouldn’t have thought it. As for the other fellow----” He handed another photograph to Tommy, and smiled at the other’s exclamation. “I’m right, then. Irishman. Prominent Unionist M.P. All a blind, of course. The 29th, you say, is the date. That gives us very little time--very little time indeed.”"}, {"paragraph": 102, "text": "“But----” Tommy hesitated."}, {"paragraph": 103, "text": "Mr. Carter read his thoughts."}, {"paragraph": 104, "text": "“We can deal with the General Strike menace, I think. But if that draft treaty turns up--we’re done. England will be plunged in anarchy. Come on, Beresford, we’ll go and have a look at this house of yours.”"}, {"paragraph": 105, "text": "Two constables were on duty in front of the house in Soho."}, {"paragraph": 106, "text": "“The birds have flown,” said Mr. Carter."}, {"paragraph": 107, "text": "Everything was just as it had been: the prison room with the crooked pictures, the broken jug in the attic. But nowhere was there a trace of papers. And there was no sign of Annette."}, {"paragraph": 108, "text": "“What you tell me about the girl puzzled me,” said Mr. Carter. “You believe that she deliberately went back?”"}, {"paragraph": 109, "text": "“It would seem so, sir. She ran upstairs while I was getting the door open.”"}, {"paragraph": 110, "text": "“H’m, she must belong to the gang, then; but, being a woman, didn’t feel like standing by to see a personable young man killed.”"}, {"paragraph": 111, "text": "“By the way,” observed Mr. Carter, “have you shown yourself to Miss Tuppence yet?”"}, {"paragraph": 112, "text": "“Tuppence? I was afraid she might get a bit rattled. Did she go to the police?”"}, {"paragraph": 113, "text": "Mr. Carter shook his head."}, {"paragraph": 114, "text": "“Then I wonder how they twigged me.”"}, {"paragraph": 115, "text": "Tommy explained. Mr. Carter nodded thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 116, "text": "“True, that’s rather a curious point. Unless the mention of the _Ritz_ was an accidental remark?”"}, {"paragraph": 117, "text": "“It might have been, sir. But they must have found out about me suddenly in some way.”"}, {"paragraph": 118, "text": "Hailing a taxi briskly Tommy was swiftly borne to the _Ritz_."}, {"paragraph": 119, "text": "“Wonder what she’s been up to. Dogging ‘Rita’ most likely. By the way, I suppose that’s who Annette meant by Marguerite. I didn’t get it at the time.” The thought saddened him a little, for it seemed to prove that Mrs. Vandemeyer and the girl were on intimate terms."}, {"paragraph": 120, "text": "The taxi drew up at the _Ritz_. Tommy burst into its sacred portals eagerly, but his enthusiasm received a check. He was informed that Miss Cowley had gone out a quarter of an hour ago."}], "019.source": [{"paragraph": 1, "text": "BAFFLED for the moment, Tommy strolled into the restaurant, and ordered
a meal of surpassing excellence. His four days’ imprisonment had taught
him anew to value good food."}, {"paragraph": 2, "text": "He was in the middle of conveying a particularly choice morsel of Sole
à la Jeanette to his mouth, when he caught sight of Julius entering
the room. Tommy waved a menu cheerfully, and succeeded in attracting the
other’s attention. At the sight of Tommy, Julius’s eyes seemed as though
they would pop out of his head. He strode across, and pump-handled
Tommy’s hand with what seemed to the latter quite unnecessary vigour."}, {"paragraph": 3, "text": "“Holy snakes!” he ejaculated. “Is it really you?”"}, {"paragraph": 4, "text": "“Of course it is. Why shouldn’t it be?”"}, {"paragraph": 5, "text": "“Why shouldn’t it be? Say, man, don’t you know you’ve been given up
for dead? I guess we’d have had a solemn requiem for you in another few
days.”"}, {"paragraph": 6, "text": "“Who thought I was dead?” demanded Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 7, "text": "“Tuppence.”"}, {"paragraph": 8, "text": "“She remembered the proverb about the good dying young, I suppose. There
must be a certain amount of original sin in me to have survived. Where
is Tuppence, by the way?”"}, {"paragraph": 9, "text": "“Isn’t she here?”"}, {"paragraph": 10, "text": "“No, the fellows at the office said she’d just gone out.”"}, {"paragraph": 11, "text": "“Gone shopping, I guess. I dropped her here in the car about an hour
ago. But, say, can’t you shed that British calm of yours, and get down
to it? What on God’s earth have you been doing all this time?”"}, {"paragraph": 12, "text": "“If you’re feeding here,” replied Tommy, “order now. It’s going to be a
long story.”"}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "Julius drew up a chair to the opposite side of the table, summoned a
hovering waiter, and dictated his wishes. Then he turned to Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "“Fire ahead. I guess you’ve had some few adventures.”"}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "“One or two,” replied Tommy modestly, and plunged into his recital."}, {"paragraph": 16, "text": "Julius listened spellbound. Half the dishes that were placed before him
he forgot to eat. At the end he heaved a long sigh."}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "“Bully for you. Reads like a dime novel!”"}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“And now for the home front,” said Tommy, stretching out his hand for a
peach."}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“We-el,” drawled Julius, “I don’t mind admitting we’ve had some
adventures too.”"}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "He, in his turn, assumed the rôle of narrator. Beginning with his
unsuccessful reconnoitring at Bournemouth, he passed on to his return
to London, the buying of the car, the growing anxieties of Tuppence,
the call upon Sir James, and the sensational occurrences of the previous
night."}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "“But who killed her?” asked Tommy. “I don’t quite understand.”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“The doctor kidded himself she took it herself,” replied Julius dryly."}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“And Sir James? What did he think?”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "“Being a legal luminary, he is likewise a human oyster,” replied Julius.
“I should say he ‘reserved judgment.’” He went on to detail the events
of the morning."}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "“Lost her memory, eh?” said Tommy with interest. “By Jove, that explains
why they looked at me so queerly when I spoke of questioning her. Bit of
a slip on my part, that! But it wasn’t the sort of thing a fellow would
be likely to guess.”"}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "“They didn’t give you any sort of hint as to where Jane was?”"}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "Tommy shook his head regretfully."}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "“Not a word. I’m a bit of an ass, as you know. I ought to have got more
out of them somehow.”"}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "“I guess you’re lucky to be here at all. That bluff of yours was the
goods all right. How you ever came to think of it all so pat beats me to
a frazzle!”"}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“I was in such a funk I had to think of something,” said Tommy simply."}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "There was a moment’s pause, and then Tommy reverted to Mrs. Vandemeyer’s
death."}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "“There’s no doubt it was chloral?”"}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "“I believe not. At least they call it heart failure induced by an
overdose, or some such claptrap. It’s all right. We don’t want to
be worried with an inquest. But I guess Tuppence and I and even the
highbrow Sir James have all got the same idea.”"}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "“Mr. Brown?” hazarded Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "“Sure thing.”"}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "Tommy nodded."}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "“All the same,” he said thoughtfully, “Mr. Brown hasn’t got wings. I
don’t see how he got in and out.”"}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“How about some high-class thought transference stunt? Some magnetic
influence that irresistibly impelled Mrs. Vandemeyer to commit suicide?”"}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "Tommy looked at him with respect."}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "“Good, Julius. Distinctly good. Especially the phraseology. But it
leaves me cold. I yearn for a real Mr. Brown of flesh and blood. I think
the gifted young detectives must get to work, study the entrances and
exits, and tap the bumps on their foreheads until the solution of the
mystery dawns on them. Let’s go round to the scene of the crime. I wish
we could get hold of Tuppence. The _Ritz_ would enjoy the spectacle of
the glad reunion.”"}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "Inquiry at the office revealed the fact that Tuppence had not yet
returned."}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "“All the same, I guess I’ll have a look round upstairs,” said Julius.
“She might be in my sitting-room.” He disappeared."}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "Suddenly a diminutive boy spoke at Tommy’s elbow:"}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "“The young lady--she’s gone away by train, I think, sir,” he murmured
shyly."}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "“What?” Tommy wheeled round upon him."}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "The small boy became pinker than before."}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "“The taxi, sir. I heard her tell the driver Charing Cross and to look
sharp.”"}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "Tommy stared at him, his eyes opening wide in surprise. Emboldened, the
small boy proceeded. “So I thought, having asked for an A.B.C. and a
Bradshaw.”"}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "Tommy interrupted him:"}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "“When did she ask for an A.B.C. and a Bradshaw?”"}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“When I took her the telegram, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "“A telegram?”"}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“Yes, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "“When was that?”"}, {"paragraph": 55, "text": "“About half-past twelve, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 56, "text": "“Tell me exactly what happened.”"}, {"paragraph": 57, "text": "The small boy drew a long breath."}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "“I took up a telegram to No. 891--the lady was there. She opened it
and gave a gasp, and then she said, very jolly like: ‘Bring me up a
Bradshaw, and an A.B.C., and look sharp, Henry.’ My name isn’t Henry,
but----”"}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "“Never mind your name,” said Tommy impatiently. “Go on.”"}, {"paragraph": 60, "text": "“Yes, sir. I brought them, and she told me to wait, and looked up
something. And then she looks up at the clock, and ‘Hurry up,’ she says.
‘Tell them to get me a taxi,’ and she begins a-shoving on of her hat in
front of the glass, and she was down in two ticks, almost as quick as I
was, and I seed her going down the steps and into the taxi, and I heard
her call out what I told you.”"}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "The small boy stopped and replenished his lungs. Tommy continued to
stare at him. At that moment Julius rejoined him. He held an open letter
in his hand."}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "“I say, Hersheimmer”--Tommy turned to him--“Tuppence has gone off
sleuthing on her own.”"}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "“Shucks!”"}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "“Yes, she has. She went off in a taxi to Charing Cross in the deuce of a
hurry after getting a telegram.” His eye fell on the letter in Julius’s
hand. “Oh; she left a note for you. That’s all right. Where’s she off
to?”"}, {"paragraph": 65, "text": "Almost unconsciously, he held out his hand for the letter, but
Julius folded it up and placed it in his pocket. He seemed a trifle
embarrassed."}, {"paragraph": 66, "text": "“I guess this is nothing to do with it. It’s about something
else--something I asked her that she was to let me know about.”"}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "“Oh!” Tommy looked puzzled, and seemed waiting for more."}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "“See here,” said Julius suddenly, “I’d better put you wise. I asked Miss
Tuppence to marry me this morning.”"}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "“Oh!” said Tommy mechanically. He felt dazed. Julius’s words were
totally unexpected. For the moment they benumbed his brain."}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "“I’d like to tell you,” continued Julius, “that before I suggested
anything of the kind to Miss Tuppence, I made it clear that I didn’t
want to butt in in any way between her and you----”"}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "Tommy roused himself."}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "“That’s all right,” he said quickly. “Tuppence and I have been pals for
years. Nothing more.” He lit a cigarette with a hand that shook ever
so little. “That’s quite all right. Tuppence always said that she was
looking out for----”"}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "He stopped abruptly, his face crimsoning, but Julius was in no way
discomposed."}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "“Oh, I guess it’ll be the dollars that’ll do the trick. Miss Tuppence
put me wise to that right away. There’s no humbug about her. We ought to
gee along together very well.”"}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "Tommy looked at him curiously for a minute, as though he were about
to speak, then changed his mind and said nothing. Tuppence and Julius!
Well, why not? Had she not lamented the fact that she knew no rich men?
Had she not openly avowed her intention of marrying for money if she
ever had the chance? Her meeting with the young American millionaire
had given her the chance--and it was unlikely she would be slow to avail
herself of it. She was out for money. She had always said so. Why blame
her because she had been true to her creed?"}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "Nevertheless, Tommy did blame her. He was filled with a passionate and
utterly illogical resentment. It was all very well to _say_ things
like that--but a _real_ girl would never marry for money. Tuppence was
utterly cold-blooded and selfish, and he would be delighted if he never
saw her again! And it was a rotten world!"}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "Julius’s voice broke in on these meditations."}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“Yes, we ought to gee along together very well. I’ve heard that a girl
always refuses you once--a sort of convention.”"}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "Tommy caught his arm."}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "“Refuses? Did you say _refuses?_”"}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "“Sure thing. Didn’t I tell you that? She just rapped out a ‘no’ without
any kind of reason to it. The eternal feminine, the Huns call it, I’ve
heard. But she’ll come round right enough. Likely enough, I hustled her
some----”"}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "But Tommy interrupted regardless of decorum."}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "“What did she say in that note?” he demanded fiercely."}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "The obliging Julius handed it to him."}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "“There’s no earthly clue in it as to where she’s gone,” he assured
Tommy. “But you might as well see for yourself if you don’t believe me.”"}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "The note, in Tuppence’s well-known schoolboy writing, ran as follows:"}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "“DEAR JULIUS,"}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "“It’s always better to have things in black and white. I don’t feel I
can be bothered to think of marriage until Tommy is found. Let’s leave
it till then."}, {"paragraph": 89, "text": "“Yours affectionately,"}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "“TUPPENCE.”"}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "Tommy handed it back, his eyes shining. His feelings had undergone a
sharp reaction. He now felt that Tuppence was all that was noble and
disinterested. Had she not refused Julius without hesitation? True, the
note betokened signs of weakening, but he could excuse that. It read
almost like a bribe to Julius to spur him on in his efforts to find
Tommy, but he supposed she had not really meant it that way. Darling
Tuppence, there was not a girl in the world to touch her! When he saw
her----His thoughts were brought up with a sudden jerk."}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "“As you say,” he remarked, pulling himself together, “there’s not a hint
here as to what she’s up to. Hi--Henry!”"}, {"paragraph": 93, "text": "The small boy came obediently. Tommy produced five shillings."}, {"paragraph": 94, "text": "“One thing more. Do you remember what the young lady did with the
telegram?”"}, {"paragraph": 95, "text": "Henry gasped and spoke."}, {"paragraph": 96, "text": "“She crumpled it up into a ball and threw it into the grate, and made a
sort of noise like ‘Whoop!’ sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 97, "text": "“Very graphic, Henry,” said Tommy. “Here’s your five shillings. Come on,
Julius. We must find that telegram.”"}, {"paragraph": 98, "text": "They hurried upstairs. Tuppence had left the key in her door. The room
was as she had left it. In the fireplace was a crumpled ball of orange
and white. Tommy disentangled it and smoothed out the telegram."}, {"paragraph": 99, "text": "“Come at once, Moat House, Ebury, Yorkshire, great developments--TOMMY.”"}, {"paragraph": 100, "text": "They looked at each other in stupefaction. Julius spoke first:"}, {"paragraph": 101, "text": "“You didn’t send it?”"}, {"paragraph": 102, "text": "“Of course not. What does it mean?”"}, {"paragraph": 103, "text": "“I guess it means the worst,” said Julius quietly. “They’ve got her.”"}, {"paragraph": 104, "text": "_“What?”_"}, {"paragraph": 105, "text": "“Sure thing! They signed your name, and she fell into the trap like a
lamb.”"}, {"paragraph": 106, "text": "“My God! What shall we do?”"}, {"paragraph": 107, "text": "“Get busy, and go after her! Right now! There’s no time to waste. It’s
almighty luck that she didn’t take the wire with her. If she had we’d
probably never have traced her. But we’ve got to hustle. Where’s that
Bradshaw?”"}, {"paragraph": 108, "text": "The energy of Julius was infectious. Left to himself, Tommy would
probably have sat down to think things out for a good half-hour before
he decided on a plan of action. But with Julius Hersheimmer about,
hustling was inevitable."}, {"paragraph": 109, "text": "After a few muttered imprecations he handed the Bradshaw to Tommy as
being more conversant with its mysteries. Tommy abandoned it in favour
of an A.B.C."}, {"paragraph": 110, "text": "“Here we are. Ebury, Yorks. From King’s Cross. Or St. Pancras. (Boy must
have made a mistake. It was King’s Cross, not _Charing_ Cross.) 12.50,
that’s the train she went by. 2.10, that’s gone. 3.20 is the next--and a
damned slow train too.”"}, {"paragraph": 111, "text": "“What about the car?”"}, {"paragraph": 112, "text": "Tommy shook his head."}, {"paragraph": 113, "text": "“Send it up if you like, but we’d better stick to the train. The great
thing is to keep calm.”"}, {"paragraph": 114, "text": "Julius groaned."}, {"paragraph": 115, "text": "“That’s so. But it gets my goat to think of that innocent young girl in
danger!”"}, {"paragraph": 116, "text": "Tommy nodded abstractedly. He was thinking. In a moment or two, he said:"}, {"paragraph": 117, "text": "“I say, Julius, what do they want her for, anyway?”"}, {"paragraph": 118, "text": "“Eh? I don’t get you?”"}, {"paragraph": 119, "text": "“What I mean is that I don’t think it’s their game to do her any harm,”
 explained Tommy, puckering his brow with the strain of his mental
processes. “She’s a hostage, that’s what she is. She’s in no immediate
danger, because if we tumble on to anything, she’d be damned useful to
